text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A group of MPs from deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party will announce they will not support a new coalition with the Islam-based Welfare Party even if Prime Minister Erbakan resigns in favour of Ciller.

- The Islamist-led coalition will end in the next few days, but all eyes are on the leader of a small right-wing party whose support is necessary if power is to be handed over smoothly to the coalition junior partner, True Path.
- An ex-Welfare Party MP is to be prosecuted for allegedly negotiating with the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) for the establishment of a Kurdish state.
- A senior Welfare MP is has started a campaign amongst deputies against support for a government headed by Ciller.
- Erbakan warned Iran over its alleged support for the PKK, during talks with Iranian president, Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani at the D-8 summit in Istanbul.
- Left-wing party leader, Deniz Baykal called for early elections to solve the government crisis rather than threats from the army.
- The government delay in implementing a free trade agreement signed with Israel last year has cost the country around $1 billion.
- International respect for Turkey has been destroyed by the artificial agenda created by the secularist media and exaggerated talk of a military coup.

- The Confederation of Public Workers' Unions (KESK) called on the other major labour confederations to make a joint demand for a general strike against the government's planned public sector wage settlement.
